name: Karawya (Caraway-Cinnamon Rice Pudding)

instructions.primary_message: For the Pudding: In a large saucepan, combine sugar, rice flour, caraway, cinnamon, ground anise, and salt. Gradually whisk in water until mixture is smooth.

Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly to prevent clumping, until mixture comes to a gentle boil. Reduce heat to medium-low and cook, whisking constantly, until thickened and glossy, about 10 minutes.

Carefully pour into serving bowls or dessert glasses, smoothing the surface with the back of a spoon or a small offset spatula. Let cool close to room temperature, 45 to 60 minutes. Refrigerate until fully set, at least 4 hours or preferably up to 24 hours.

To Soak the Nuts (optional): While pudding is cooling, combine walnuts, almonds, and pine nuts in a small bowl. Pour cold water over nuts to cover. Allow to soak until plump and softened, about 30 minutes.
Divide coconut evenly over chilled karawya. Top decoratively with pistachios, walnuts, almonds, and pine nuts, if using. Serve.

schema_metadata.keywords: karawya pudding, caraway pudding, cinnamon pudding, cinnamon dessert, rice pudding, spiced pudding

description: Karawya is a Levantine rice flour pudding spiced with caraway, cinnamon, and anise, then topped with coconut and nuts for a celebratory dessert.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 4 hr 20 min.

Optional or for serving: 25 g untoasted walnuts (about 1/4 cup), chopped into large pieces (optional); 18 g (about 2 tablespoons) blanched, untoasted almonds (optional); 8 g (about 2 teaspoons) untoasted pine nuts (optional)

Notes: Use white rice flour (such as Bob's Red Mill); glutinous rice flour will produce a sticky texture.
Caraway may be purchased pre-ground or freshly ground from whole seeds.
Using all the nut varieties is encouraged, but if omitting the walnuts, almonds, or pine nuts, increase the pistachios to make up the difference.

Make-ahead and storage: Pudding can be made up to 4 days in advance; cover individual portions with plastic wrap and store in the refrigerator. Top with coconut and nuts after pudding has set.
author: Laila Ibrahim
